record.paper_title: Exchange Bias and Interface-related Effects in Two-dimensional van der Waals Magnetic Heterostructures: Open Questions and Perspectives
record.original_question: In Fe3GeTe2/CrCl3 van der Waals heterostructures, is exchange bias caused purely by direct ferromagnet/antiferromagnet coupling, or is it altered by an interfacial oxide or spin-cluster layer, magnetic proximity between Fe3GeTe2 and CrCl3, and charge transfer across the interface?

evidence.quote: If the oxide phase was present between the Fe3GeTe2 and CrCl3 layers and behaved as "spin clusters", then the AFM CrCl3 could act as a pinning layer and the EB mechanism would be different from what was proposed.
MP and its impact on magnetism and EB should thus be systematically investigated in these heterostructures.

In addition, charge transfer between Fe3GeTe2 and CrCl3 could give rise to the enhanced magnetism in Fe3GeTe2 and hence the EB effect in the Fe3GeTe2/CrCl3 heterostructure, which should also be investigated further.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a van der Waals magnetic heterostructure obtained by stacking a thin flake of the itinerant ferromagnet Fe₃GeTe₂ (FGT) on top of (or beneath) a thin flake of the layered antiferromagnet CrCl₃, where CrCl₃ has ferromagnetic intralayer order and antiferromagnetic interlayer order below its Néel temperature. After field-cooling such a heterostructure, the hysteresis loop of the FGT layer is shifted along the field axis by an amount H_EB ≠ 0, a phenomenon known as exchange bias (EB).

Identify the microscopic origin of this exchange bias by determining, in a quantitative and mechanism-resolving manner, the relative contributions of the following four candidate effects:

(a) Direct interfacial exchange coupling between the ferromagnetic FGT spins and the uncompensated antiferromagnetic CrCl₃ spins at the shared van der Waals interface, treated as the conventional ferromagnet/antiferromagnet pinning mechanism.

(b) The presence of an interfacial oxide (or otherwise disordered) phase at the FGT/CrCl₃ interface that behaves as a layer of magnetic "spin clusters," with CrCl₃ then acting as a secondary pinning layer for these clusters rather than directly for FGT.

(c) Magnetic proximity coupling, in which the electronic wavefunctions of FGT and CrCl₃ hybridize across the van der Waals gap and induce modifications of the magnetization profile (e.g., interfacial spin polarization, exchange splitting, and altered anisotropy) in both layers.

(d) Interfacial charge transfer between FGT and CrCl₃, which can renormalize the carrier density and exchange interactions in FGT (possibly enhancing its Curie temperature and magnetization) and thereby influence the exchange bias.

The problem is: starting from a microscopic model of the FGT/CrCl₃ interface (including the possibility of an interfacial oxide/spin-cluster layer, proximity-induced exchange, and charge redistribution), derive H_EB(T, t_FGT, t_CrCl₃, H_FC) as a function of temperature, layer thicknesses, and cooling field, and decompose it into the contributions of mechanisms (a)–(d); equivalently, determine whether the observed exchange bias in FGT/CrCl₃ heterostructures is due purely to mechanism (a) or whether mechanisms (b), (c), and/or (d) make essential contributions.
artifact.category_tag: van der Waals magnetic heterostructures / exchange bias
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature indicates that the microscopic mechanism of exchange bias in Fe3GeTe2/CrCl3 (and related FGT-based) heterostructures remains unresolved. Subsequent works have shown that surface oxidation of Fe3GeTe2 alone produces exchange bias via an antiferromagnetic surface oxide, and studies on CrPS4/Fe3GeTe2 explicitly invoke interfacial-oxide modulation; magnetic proximity and charge-transfer contributions are acknowledged but not quantitatively disentangled. No definitive decomposition of the four contributions has been established.

status_evidence.title: Exchange Bias in van der Waals CrCl3/Fe3GeTe2 Heterostructures
status_evidence.snippet: Exchange-bias fields over 50 mT in CrCl3/Fe3GeTe2 at 2.5 K, tunable by field-cooling and thickness.
status_evidence.claim: Reports EB in FGT/CrCl3 but does not uniquely identify its microscopic origin.

status_evidence.title: Exchange Bias in Weakly Interlayer-Coupled van der Waals Magnet Fe3GeTe2
status_evidence.snippet: Naturally oxidized Fe3GeTe2 exhibits exchange bias attributed to AFM coupling of surface oxide with unoxidized FGT.
status_evidence.claim: Surface oxidation of FGT itself yields EB, suggesting oxide/spin-cluster mechanisms can dominate.

status_evidence.title: Harnessing van der Waals CrPS4 and Surface Oxides for non-monotonic pre-set field induced Exchange Bias in Fe3GeTe2
status_evidence.snippet: Interfacial oxide modulates EB in CrPS4/Fe3GeTe2 heterostructures.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms interfacial-oxide pathway as an active EB mechanism in FGT/2D-AFM systems.
